questions.stem: On a price tag, a test-taker traces one phrase before answering. What is the Italian plural of "spiaggia"?
questions.explanation: The singular noun "spiaggia" forms its plural as "spiagge". Italian nouns change their ending to mark number, and the article changes in tandem to agree with the new plural form.
questions.hint: Recall how nouns of this gender and ending form their plural.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: In a practice quiz, an examiner singles out one form for the check. Choose the subjunctive: "loro tornare".

options.misconception: this is the io form of the verb, not loro
this is the noi form of the verb, not loro
this is the voi form of the verb, not loro

questions.explanation: The subjunctive form of "tornare" for "loro" is "tornino". The present subjunctive is used after expressions of doubt, wish, or necessity. It draws its stem from the third-person plural present. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the subjunctive ending for that person.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: A dialogue lists one answer before the test. What does the negative word "niente" mean?
questions.explanation: The Italian negative word "niente" means "nothing" in English. Italian negation often requires the particle non before the verb together with a negative word, a structure known as double negation.
questions.hint: Decide whether this word denies an action, a person, or a thing.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.learningObjective: Identify the infinitive behind a conjugated form
questions.stem: Which infinitive does the form "ho" come from?
questions.explanation: The form "ho" is the present form for "io" of "avere". Identifying the infinitive behind a conjugated form requires matching the stem and the person endings to the correct conjugation pattern.
questions.hint: Strip the ending and match the remaining stem to an infinitive.
